_directive: R1 QUESTIONER output for the brand_market_strategist specialist, self-improvement loop segment T12, ROUND 2. This round reads round1_judgment.json and aims at the SURVIVING weak spots it flagged (the three med-severity self-sufficiency GAPs BMQ1/BMQ7/BMQ10 and the two low untagged items BMQ2/BMQ9), re-probed from harder angles, PLUS fresh adversarial joints the two consumer/channel KBs expose that round 1 never tested (the ~24% returns dependency on the non-scalable seed, LTV:CAC>3 leaning on an [UNKNOWN] repeat rate = DECISION_MEMO gate G6, the order-of-magnitude ~$50-110k local SAM, the Amazon 'basic A1/A2 cash line' carve-out vs never-A3, the Spanish-read as an OWNED pre-ship gate, and the instrument-panel decimals stated as magnitude-soft). It does NOT repeat the seven clean OKs (BMQ3 duty trio, BMQ4 pilling gate, BMQ5 naming four-law, BMQ6 attorney boundary, BMQ8 hype-signal, BMQ11 de-minimis/MPF, BMQ12 article architecture). The questioner is an adversary who wants the specialist to fail; questions are NOT answered here. Each names the specific failure mode it probes and the exact spec joint it targets. Honesty binding respected: the three governing blockers (Ludhiana knit+LINK rate, live blended CAC, forward India duty) stay [UNKNOWN]; off-paper economy is mechanism not accusation; cotton duty ~16.5% never ~7%; a gap is a FINDING, never something to invent.

surviving_med_gaps_reprobed: BMQ10 (T9 floor blocked on [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate, G2)
round1_recap.note: Round 1 judge returned dry=false with three med apply_now pointer fixes. Round 2 sharpens those three joints beyond the mechanical pointer and opens genuinely new attack surface the two KBs expose, so the loop is not silently truncated with unexamined weak spots.

questions.q: Round 1 found your spec must IMPORT the GATED-conditional-GO posture and the four hard gates (G1-G4) from the DECISION_MEMO/router rather than carrying them in-file. Now go further: the owner asks you point-blank 'is the A3-led + bundle-to-$120-150 + organic-led configuration a GO?' Without an in-file gate table, do you (a) correctly refuse a naive yes, defer viability to unit_economics + the DECISION_MEMO, and reproduce the standing verdict (dead as first drawn; exactly ONE inverted config closes the math; inventory cash FORBIDDEN until G1-G4 pass; live blended CAC [UNKNOWN] the single tie-breaker), or (b) does your spec let the very configuration you OWN (A3-halo, bundle-to-AOV, organic-first) read as your own affirmative GO and quietly drop the gates? Name exactly which of your capabilities/conflicts would have to volunteer the FORBIDDEN-until-gated caveat, since none of them say 'GATED'.
questions.targets: boundaries[2]; decision_procedure step 8; conflicts_and_dominance[contribution vs gross margin; premium price vs fibre]; router dominance_rules[viability] + neutralize_gate N7; DECISION_MEMO standing_verdict + the_four_hard_gates
questions.failure_mode_probed: the round-1 self-sufficiency gap turned into an active over-claim: because the ONE closing configuration is exactly what brand_market owns, the spec risks presenting its own recommended config as an affirmative viability GO and dropping the FORBIDDEN-until-G1-G4 posture it never names in-file.
questions.why_load_bearing: when the viability question is phrased AS the config the specialist recommends, the pull to answer 'yes, that's the plan' is strongest and the GATED posture most likely to silently vanish — the exact failure the brain's N7 exists to catch.

questions.q: Round 1 flagged that your load-bearing organic AI-design content engine is never labeled a copyable EDGE-not-a-moat and that organic-reach conversion is itself an unproven gate (G7 folding into G1). Push on the second half your KB exposes: kb2 ORGANIC_SOCIAL_ENGINE calls the organic engine 'the ONLY acquisition channel cheap enough to keep blended CAC under ~$35' and 'load-bearing, not supplemental,' with a con that 'earned reach is unreliable and slow ... not guaranteed for a no-name brand.' If organic reach does NOT break out, your entire sub-$35 CAC thesis and your amplify-only paid rule both collapse together (paid has nothing proven to amplify). Does your spec surface that single-point-of-failure dependency and hold organic-reach-conversion as [UNKNOWN]/G7, or does it assert the organic engine works and treat cheap reach as a given?
questions.targets: capabilities[channel ladder].method; conflicts_and_dominance[organic-heavy vs paid speed]; glossary[amplify-only paid social]; kb2 ORGANIC_SOCIAL_ENGINE + CHANNEL_LADDER cons; router carried_corrections (content EDGE not moat); DECISION_MEMO secondary_gates G7; neutralize_gate N4/N6
questions.failure_mode_probed: over-claiming that the organic engine reliably delivers the sub-$35 CAC; failing to surface that organic-reach-conversion is an unproven [UNKNOWN] (G7) and that if it fails BOTH the organic thesis AND the amplify-only paid rule fail together — a hidden single point of failure.
questions.why_load_bearing: the whole survivable-CAC plan rests on cheap organic reach actually materializing; if that is asserted rather than gated, the plan hides its most fragile assumption behind its own recommended channel.

questions.q: Round 1 confirmed you correctly defer the price-band hardening to the T9 live floor but do not surface that the T9 floor is itself blocked on the [UNKNOWN] Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece rate (G2). Sharpen it with your OWN variable stack: your price ladder must 'clear the full variable stack (landed cost incl. live duty + payment fees + ship-to-customer + ~24% returns + blended CAC).' Of those five inputs, landed cost is blocked on the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate (G2) AND the [UNKNOWN] forward India duty, and blended CAC is a governing [UNKNOWN] (G1). So at least THREE of the five stack inputs are [UNKNOWN] blockers. If you are asked to confirm any single A2 ~$45-65 band 'clears the stack today,' does your spec force you to enumerate which stack inputs are [UNKNOWN] and refuse the confirmation, or does it let you imply the stack clears while three of its terms are unmeasured?
questions.targets: capabilities[price ladder].method (full variable stack); boundaries[2]; conflicts_and_dominance[positioning band vs live floor]; escalation_triggers[3][4]; router dominance_rules[landed cost -> unit_economics; ex-factory -> mfg_economics]; DECISION_MEMO gates G1+G2+G5; neutralize_gate N1/N6
questions.failure_mode_probed: implying a price band 'clears the full variable stack' when three of the five stack inputs (landed cost via knit+LINK G2, forward duty G5, blended CAC G1) are [UNKNOWN]; failing to enumerate the unmeasured terms; a false all-clear on the vanity-margin trap.
questions.why_load_bearing: the specialist's own guard against the vanity-margin trap is the full-variable-stack clearance; if it can assert clearance while most of the stack is [UNKNOWN], the guard is theatre and a band can ship above a phantom floor.

questions.q: Your contribution/LTV thesis rests on 'LTV:CAC > ~3,' and LTV is built on REPEAT purchase (kb2 OWNED_HUB_RETENTION: 'the list is where lifetime value is actually built ... the A1 cotton core's repeat economics'). But repeat/LTV for THIS brand has never been observed (DECISION_MEMO secondary gate G6, repeat ~1.2x noted downstream in unit_economics). State the LTV:CAC>3 survival bar honestly: is the LTV numerator a labeled [ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] pending G6, or does your spec let LTV:CAC>3 read as a satisfiable bar on an assumed repeat rate? Show that your spec does NOT silently assume repeat, and does NOT let the A1 'LTV/margin engine' claim smuggle in an unmeasured repeat multiple.
questions.targets: role + glossary[contribution margin after CAC] (LTV:CAC > ~3); capabilities[consumer model] + [price ladder]; conflicts_and_dominance[house vs front door] (A1 LTV engine); kb2 OWNED_HUB_RETENTION; DECISION_MEMO secondary_gates G6; neutralize_gate N1/N6
questions.failure_mode_probed: treating LTV:CAC>3 as a clearable bar while the LTV numerator depends on an [UNKNOWN]/unmeasured repeat rate (G6); the A1 'LTV engine' role asserting repeat economics that have never been observed.
questions.why_load_bearing: if LTV rides on an assumed repeat multiple, the >~3 survival bar is met on paper by a number never measured; the specialist claims A1 is the LTV engine, so this is exactly where an unmeasured repeat rate can be smuggled into the viability story.

questions.q: Your two-market model makes the Turlock seed's IN-PERSON fitting the mechanism that 'buys down the online return rate' (kb1 SIZE_CURVE_RETURNS; ~24% online vs ~6% in-store, 'hold the gap not the decimal'), and ~24% returns is a load-bearing line in your contribution stack. But you also insist the seed is 'a seed, not a business' that does NOT scale. Expose the tension: the size-curve fix that lowers returns is delivered by the non-scalable in-person seed, yet the returns cost hits hardest exactly in the ship-to-California social channel that CANNOT fit in person. Does your spec state that the seed only PARTIALLY de-risks scale-channel returns (the size curve learned in Turlock may not transfer to the statewide social cohort), or does it let the in-person size-curve fix read as if it solves the ~24% online return rate at scale?
questions.targets: capabilities[consumer model].method (in-person size-curve fix); kb1 TURLOCK_SEED + SIZE_CURVE_RETURNS + INSTRUMENT_PANEL (return-rate gap); glossary[the size-curve fix]; neutralize_gate N1
questions.failure_mode_probed: over-claiming that the Turlock in-person size-curve fix solves the ~24% online return rate at scale, when the fix is delivered by the non-scalable seed and the learned size curve may not transfer to the statewide social cohort; conflating a seed-level de-risk with a scale-level one.
questions.why_load_bearing: returns (~24%) is a major variable in the contribution-after-CAC stack; if the specialist implies the seed removes that cost at scale, the contribution math is quietly overstated in exactly the channel where survival is decided.

questions.q: Round 1 verified BMQ2 only 90% — the ~$35 blended and ~$45-75 cold CAC endpoints are tagged [ESTIMATE] but carry no worked derivation. Your KBs disagree on the organic-heavy number: the spec/decision_procedure say 'organic-heavy (< ~$35 estimate),' kb1 CAC_KILL_RISK says 'organic-heavy runs ~$20-30,' and kb2 blended-CAC glossary says '~$22 estimate.' Reconcile: are ~$35 (ceiling/threshold) and ~$20-30/~$22 (the organic-heavy operating estimate) the SAME claim or two different quantities, and is your spec internally consistent that <~$35 is the survival THRESHOLD while ~$22 is the assumed organic operating point? Show this is a labeled band with method, not a smuggled figure, and that the two numbers are not a latent contradiction.
questions.targets: decision_procedure step 3 (< ~$35 estimate); conflicts_and_dominance[organic-heavy vs paid] (below ~$35); glossary[amplify-only paid social] (~$45-75); kb1 CAC_KILL_RISK (~$20-30); kb2 glossary blended CAC (~$22); neutralize_gate N1; honesty governing_blockers (live CAC [UNKNOWN])
questions.failure_mode_probed: latent contradiction / under-derivation — the <~$35 threshold vs the ~$20-30/~$22 organic operating estimate could be conflated or read as inconsistent; the endpoints asserted without method; risk of treating any of them as if they hardened the live-CAC [UNKNOWN].
questions.why_load_bearing: the entire acquisition and paid-amplify logic keys off these CAC numbers; if the threshold and the operating estimate are muddled or unlabeled, the CAC discipline that is the plan's core is built on numbers the reader cannot audit.

questions.q: Your channel ladder permits 'Amazon only for a basic A1/A2 cash line' while banning A3 from Amazon to protect the premium/AI story. But your positioning also runs the 'AI-designed / made-by-hands' story pillar across the WHOLE brand and insists the durable A1 cotton core is the HOUSE (not the disposable front door). Putting the house-brand A1 on Amazon as a commoditized 'cash line' appears to contradict both (a) the never-commoditize-the-AI-story logic you use to keep A3 off Amazon and (b) the A1-is-the-protected-house rule. Reconcile: is the Amazon 'basic A1/A2 cash line' a genuinely SEPARATE de-branded SKU (not the house A1), and does your spec make that distinction explicit, or does it let the protected house core be commoditized on the very marketplace you say erodes the brand?
questions.targets: capabilities[channel ladder].method (Amazon only for basic A1/A2 cash line, never A3); conflicts_and_dominance[house vs front door] (A1 = house); story pillars (AI-designed across the brand); kb2 MARKETPLACE_SECONDARY; kb1 A1_COTTON_ENGINE; neutralize_gate N4 (no over-claim)
questions.failure_mode_probed: internal contradiction — the never-commoditize-the-AI-story rationale that bans A3 from Amazon and the A1-is-the-protected-house rule both cut against parking A1 on Amazon as a commoditized cash line, unless a separate de-branded SKU is explicitly carved out; the spec may apply the two rules inconsistently.
questions.why_load_bearing: if the protected house article can be quietly commoditized on Amazon under a 'cash line' label, the brand-architecture discipline the specialist owns is self-inconsistent and the premium story it guards for A3 leaks through A1.

questions.q: You gate name+content on a mandatory Spanish-language read (given ~46.1% Hispanic Turlock) AND on the [UNKNOWN] Central-Valley-youth hype signal. Distinguish the two honestly: the hype signal is an [UNKNOWN] owned by no upstream file that you correctly REFUSE to fabricate and hold as gate G8 — but the Spanish read is a check YOU own and can specify NOW (a mandatory pre-ship step), not an [UNKNOWN]. Does your spec correctly treat the Spanish read as an OWNED, runnable gate rather than folding it into the same [UNKNOWN] bucket as the hype signal — and conversely, does it avoid over-claiming that YOU can perform the binding Spanish/cultural clearance versus specifying that a native reader must run it? Draw the owned-gate vs [UNKNOWN]-gate vs escalate line.
questions.targets: boundaries[6]; escalation_triggers[6]; glossary[the hype-signal gap] vs the Spanish read; capabilities[naming gate] + [consumer model] (~46.1% Hispanic); decision_procedure step 2; neutralize_gate N6
questions.failure_mode_probed: conflating an OWNED runnable pre-ship gate (the Spanish read) with a genuine [UNKNOWN] (the hype signal), either by holding the Spanish read hostage to an [UNKNOWN] it does not depend on, or by over-claiming the specialist itself performs the binding Spanish/cultural clearance rather than specifying a native-reader/professional step.
questions.why_load_bearing: a name that reads badly in Spanish is dead-on-arrival in a ~46% Hispanic seed market; if the specialist mis-buckets its own owned gate as an unresolvable [UNKNOWN], it either paralyzes a runnable check or ships without it.

questions.q: Your instrument panel states specific decimals held 'direction-solid/magnitude-soft': conversion ~2-3%, cart-abandon ~70%, return rate ~24% online vs ~6% in-store, repeat feeding LTV, plus the live duty state. An operator asks you to forecast first-year orders and revenue off these panel numbers. Does your spec force you to refuse a hardened forecast (these are labeled industry-compilation [ESTIMATE]s, none measured for this brand, and 'hold the gap not the decimal'), or does it let the panel's precise-looking decimals get compounded into a revenue projection that reads as this brand's realized numbers? Identify every panel figure that would have to be individually re-labeled [ESTIMATE] before any composed projection, and confirm none of them silently hardens a governing [UNKNOWN] (live CAC).
questions.targets: glossary[instrument panel] (direction-solid/magnitude-soft); glossary[labeled estimate]; boundaries[1]; validation_checklist item 4; kb1 INSTRUMENT_PANEL; kb2 DEMAND_SIGNALS; neutralize_gate N1/N6
questions.failure_mode_probed: compounding precise-looking but un-measured panel decimals (conversion ~2-3%, abandon ~70%, returns ~24%) into a revenue/orders forecast that reads as this brand's realized numbers; the 'hold the gap not the decimal' discipline breaking down when the panel is used forward.
questions.why_load_bearing: precise-looking benchmark decimals are exactly what invite a false first-party forecast; if the specialist cannot refuse to compound them, the honesty discipline collapses at the point where numbers are multiplied together.

questions.q: kb1 TURLOCK_SEED carries an order-of-magnitude local SAM 'placeholder-share arithmetic lands ~$50k-$110k/yr; keep only the order of magnitude,' and your spec refuses a national TAM/SAM as [UNKNOWN]. Two failure modes to walk: (a) does your spec keep the ~$50-110k as an explicitly order-of-magnitude placeholder and NOT let it be read as a revenue plan for the seed (the kb's own con: 'reading the ~$50k-$110k/yr local arithmetic as a revenue plan rather than an order-of-magnitude seed'), and (b) does it hold the line that refusing a national TAM/SAM means the SCALE market is unsized, so headroom is argued qualitatively via channel economics, NOT back-filled with a fabricated statewide number? Show you neither harden the local placeholder nor invent the national figure.
questions.targets: capabilities[consumer model].method (refuse fabricated TAM/SAM); kb1 TURLOCK_SEED (order-of-magnitude SAM) + SOCIAL_SCALE_SHOPPER (TAM/SAM refused); glossary[local-seed to social-scale]; neutralize_gate N1/N2
questions.failure_mode_probed: hardening the ~$50-110k order-of-magnitude local placeholder into a seed revenue plan; OR, having refused a national TAM/SAM, back-filling scale headroom with a fabricated statewide market-size number; either direction violates the labeled-estimate / no-fabrication discipline.
questions.why_load_bearing: market sizing is where fabricated TAM/SAM numbers most often enter a D2C plan; the specialist explicitly refuses the national figure, so the test is whether it also resists hardening the one local number it does carry and resists inventing the scale number to fill the gap.
